summary: Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004 under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a Lecturer in Sanskrit Studies at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010).
Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, he served as Coordinator of the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and later held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki is a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his MSc, DPhil, and DLitt at Oxford. He taught Japanese at the University of Tasmania, was associate professor at Kyoto University, and became Emeritus Professor at Cambridge (~1985–2017).

Peter Friedlander specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (1983–1991) and served as Associate Professor at the Australian National University in 2013.

Peter Gaeffke was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in 1952. He served as Professor at Utrecht University (1965–1975) and at the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gerlitz was a scholar of religious studies who studied under Friedrich Heiler from around 1950 to 1954. He held a post at the University of Bremen from approximately 1974 to 1991.

Peter Giles was a linguist who studied at King's College London, Aberdeen, Cambridge, Freiburg, and Leipzig. He served as a classical tutor (1887) and Fellow and Lecturer (1911) at Emmanuel College, and as Reader in Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1891).
Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics by 1990 and held an adjunct post at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Hartmann was a linguist, Indologist, and Japanologist who earned his PhD at the University of Münster under Alfred Schmitt in 1950. He became Professor of General and IE Linguistics at Münster in 1956 and Professor of General Linguistics at Konstanz in 1969.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and was Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland, where he served from 1976 to 2011.
Peter Haskel specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his PhD at Yale University (~1956–1961). He taught at Yale, Vassar College, the University of Washington, and Bennington College before holding a post at the University of Otago from approximately 1971 to 1999.

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and earned his PhD at the Australian National University (attested 2010) under doctoral supervisor John Powers alongside several traditional teachers.

Peter K. Austin is a linguist who completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He served as Foundation Professor in Linguistics at the University of Melbourne (1996–2002) and Emeritus Professor in Field Linguistics at SOAS (2002–2018).
Peter Koret specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and has held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993). He held academic posts at the University of Düsseldorf (~1999–2002), the University of Giessen (~2002–2007), and the University of Göttingen (~2007).
